newsitem.title: LEBANON: Banque Audi steams ahead in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Banque Audi steams ahead in Beirut.

text.p: Bank Audi rose $1 for the second successive day on Thursday, reaching $22 on the Beirut Stock Exchange in heavy demand.
The rise brought to 47 percent Banque Audi's increase since listing in January at $15.
Brokers said the shares were following the rise of the bank's GDRs which currently stand at $24.25-$24.75 on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange.
"If Audi's GDR holds at its current price or goes higher, then the shares will go up closer to the GDR," a broker who asked not to be identified said.
Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce fell slightly to $16.375 from $16.5 on profit-taking, brokers said. Bank of Beirut was unchanged at $3.5625.
The LIBX bank index rose 1.31 percent to 141.49. The LISPI and BLOM general indices rose 0.95 percent and 1.1 percent to 87.22 and 925.49 respectively.
Solidere A shares rebounded, rising to $10.5 from $10.25 and B shares were unchanged at $10.75.
Of the four industrial companies listed, pipemaker Eternit rose to $2 from $1.96875 on Tuesday when they were last traded. Turnover was low at 2,440 shares.
Ciments Libanais rose to $1.25 from $1.21875 at their last trade on Tuesday. Turnover was 155 shares.
Total market turnover was 128,657 shares for a value of $1,316,352 compared with 142,330 shares for a value of $1,355,603 on Thursday.
There was no trade in Ciments Blancs or Uniceramic.
